export.itsPublicKeysWhichOthers: Its public keys, which others use to encrypt to it and to check its signatures.

export.keysOthersCanUseTo.other: {count} keys others can use to add it to conversations, {size}.

export.keysToMessagesSentBefore: Keys to messages sent before you joined a group, encrypted for you.
export.madeFromYourPasswordOn: Made from your password on your device. The server checks sign-ins against it.
export.messagesFilesReactionsCallsAnd: Messages, files, reactions, calls and voice are encrypted on your device for the people in the conversation, and kept only as the sizes above.
export.signInsThatHaventAdded: Sign-ins that haven't added a device yet.
export.theCurrentSixHourPeriod: The current six-hour period began {when}. Deleted once they expire.
export.theLastEachOneIsSigned: The last {when}. Each one is signed by the keys before it. This happens when a device is removed or your password changes.
export.theSameForYourRecovery: The same, for your recovery key.
export.theServerKnowsWhosIn: The server knows who's in each conversation, when they joined, and when and how much is sent. What's said, who said it, and group and channel names are encrypted.
export.theServerSeesItWith: The server sees it with each request, and counts requests from each address in memory for up to a day to stop flooding. It never saves it, though a proxy in front of the server might log it, and the voice server also sees it during calls. If you set a SOCKS5 proxy on a device, the server sees the proxy's address instead.
export.theirNamesAndAudioAre: Their names and audio are encrypted.
export.theirNamesAndTopicsAre: Their names and topics are encrypted.
export.theseNeverReachTheServer: These never reach the server, or reach it only in a form it can't read or tie to you.
export.theyreSentWithoutYourAccount: They're sent without your account attached. Who wrote them is signed inside, where only the people in the conversation can see it.
export.thisHappensWhenADevice: This happens when a device is removed or your password changes.
export.whatTheServerChecksYour: What the server checks your password and recovery key against. It can't be turned back into them. It's left out of this export, because anyone with a copy could use it to test guesses at your password.
export.whatYouWriteSendAnd: What you write, send and say
export.whoSentEachMessageReaction: Who sent each message, reaction or pin
export.whoYouBlockAndWhat: Who you block and what you pin
export.yourAccountKeyEncryptedFor: Your account key, encrypted for it, {size}.
export.yourAccountKeyEncryptedSo: Your account key, encrypted so only your password can unlock it.
export.yourAccountKeyEncryptedSoOnly: Your account key, encrypted so only your recovery key can unlock it.
export.yourAccountsOwnRecord: Your account's own record. The server can read your username, your role and the times. Your name, bio and picture are in your profile, which it can't read.
export.yourDevicesAndTheirKeys: Your devices and their keys, made public so the server can't show different people different keys.
export.yourDevicesAreGivenTokens: Your devices are given tokens that are spent on each message, reaction and edit. Once spent, a token can't be traced back to whoever it was given to, so the server can't tell which messages are yours.
export.yourDisplayNameBioAnd: Your display name, bio and the key to your picture, encrypted so only people on this server can read them.
export.yourIdentityKeyWhichThe: Your identity key, which the emoji people compare come from, and the key others use to encrypt to you, with their signatures.
export.yourSettingsYourChatList: Your settings, your chat list, who you block, the keys to earlier messages and what you've saved, encrypted so only your devices can read it.

security.keyChanged: The security key of {name} changed. Their messages can't be trusted until you verify them again.
security.keyMismatch: The security key of {name} doesn't match the one your account knows. Their messages can't be trusted until you verify them again.
security.keysForAConversationsHistory: Keys for a conversation's history weren't signed by one of its admins, so they were ignored.
security.kindChanged: The server tried to pass one of your conversations off as a different kind of conversation. Zuna didn't go along with it.
security.logBack: The server's record of who holds which keys was rolled back, or the server is hiding part of it from this device. Compare emoji with the people who matter to you.
security.logEra: The server restarted its record of who holds which keys, as can happen after restoring a backup. Nothing this device trusts has changed.
security.logLink: The server's record of who holds which keys doesn't match the one the invite link you joined with saw. Someone may be posing as people on this server. Compare emoji with the people who matter to you.
security.logManifest: The server's record of who holds which keys doesn't match what your other devices saw. Someone may be posing as people you talk to. Compare emoji with the people who matter to you.
security.logNameTaken: The server registered someone else under your username. Apps will ignore that account, but compare emoji with the people who matter to you.
security.logOdd: Part of the server's record of who holds which keys doesn't make sense, and was ignored.
security.logOwnHistory: The server showed this device a different history of your account's keys. Someone may be trying to take over your account.
security.logOwnLeftOut: The server left this device out of its record of who holds which keys, so the people you message won't accept messages from it.
security.logProof: The server showed different people different records of who holds which keys. Someone may be posing as people you talk to. Compare emoji with the people who matter to you.
security.logServerKey: The server signed its record of who holds which keys with a key this device doesn't recognize. Nothing new in it was accepted.
security.logUnfit: The server's record of who holds which keys is inconsistent. Nothing new in it was accepted.
security.logWithheld: The server is hiding part of its record of someone's keys from this device.

serverSettings.ban.text: They're signed out everywhere and removed from every group and channel. An admin can unban them later, in Bans.
serverSettings.ban.title: Ban {name}?
serverSettings.bans.lead: People banned from {server}. Once unbanned, they can sign in again and get their direct messages and channels back. Groups will have to add them again.
serverSettings.bans.ownerOnly: Only the server's owner can unban an admin.
serverSettings.delete.confirmText: It can't be undone. Messages you sent stay with the people you sent them to, shown as from "Deleted account".
serverSettings.delete.lead: This deletes your account on {server}, with your profile and keys, signs out your other devices, and erases this device's copy of your messages. Messages you sent stay with the people you sent them to, shown as from "Deleted account". Someone else will be able to take your username. It can't be undone.
serverSettings.delete.ownerLead: You own {server}, and a server can't exist without its owner, so you can't delete your account there. To remove everything, shut down the server and delete its data.
serverSettings.emotes.lead: Everyone on this server shares one 7TV emote set. Your server downloads and caches the images, so 7TV never sees your members' IP addresses. It checks 7TV for changes to the set every few hours.
serverSettings.emotes.linkHint: Paste a link to any emote set on 7TV.
serverSettings.invites.lead: Invite links are the safest way for people to join.
serverSettings.invites.openSignUpsHint: Anyone who knows the address can join. This gives the server the key that protects profiles, so it can read display names and pictures. Messages stay encrypted.
serverSettings.leave.action: Sign out and erase local data
serverSettings.leave.lead: This signs you out of {server} on this device and erases its local copy of your messages. Your account and history stay on the server, and you can sign back in with your password.
serverSettings.overview.addressHint: The address people and apps use to reach your server.
serverSettings.overview.lead: The name and picture are public: they appear on invite pages before anyone signs in.
serverSettings.overview.name: Server name
serverSettings.overview.title: Server
serverSettings.reports.lead: People reported by others on {server}, and why. Messages are encrypted, so nobody here can see what was said, and who made each report isn't kept.
serverSettings.storage.retentionHint: 0 keeps messages forever. Pinned messages are kept. This is enforced by the server, so it only removes the server's copy.

settings.about.encryption: Messages use MLS (RFC 9420) through the independently audited OpenMLS library. Your server stores only ciphertext.
settings.about.version: Version {version} · Free software under the AGPL-3.0 license
settings.appearance.enterToSendHint: If off, use Ctrl+Enter to send and Enter for new lines.
settings.appearance.languageHintBrowser: Zuna follows your browser's language unless you pick one.
settings.data.footnote: This is what {server} says it keeps. A modified server could keep more than it says, which is why everything that matters is encrypted on your devices before it's sent.
settings.data.lead: Everything {server} says it keeps about your account. Your messages, name, picture and files are encrypted on your devices before they're sent, so only their sizes appear here.
settings.devices.addDevice: To add a device, sign in on it at {address}
settings.devices.title: Your devices on this server
settings.notifications.blockedByBrowser: Your browser is blocking notifications from this site. Allow them in your browser's site settings.
settings.notifications.desktopHint: If you're using another device, they wait 30 seconds and won't show if you read the chat there.
settings.notifications.lead: Previews are decrypted on this device. No notification service ever sees them.
settings.notifications.previewHint: Choose less if others can see your screen.
settings.privacy.blockedEmpty: Nobody yet. You can block someone from their details in a chat, or from a group's member list.
settings.privacy.blockedHint: You won't see messages from people you block or get notified about them. They aren't told, and your server can't see who you block.
settings.privacy.keepMetadataNote: Your server still can't see any of it, since files are encrypted. This only applies to this device, and to files you send from now on.
settings.privacy.keepMetadataText: Photos and videos from phones usually record where they were taken, to within a few meters, and when. With this off, everyone in a chat you send them to can see that, along with the camera or phone and its serial number, the software used, and how it was edited. So can anyone they forward the files to.
settings.privacy.lead: These apply to {server}. Each server you join has its own settings.
settings.privacy.linkPreviewsHint: When you type a link, this device loads the page to get its title and picture, and sends them encrypted with your message. The site sees your IP address, just as when you open a link. Your server never sees it.
settings.privacy.playYouTubeHint: People in a voice channel or call can watch YouTube videos together. When you watch one, it plays from YouTube, which sees your IP address and which video it is. Nothing is loaded from YouTube until you press Watch. If this is off, Zuna asks you first.
settings.privacy.readReceiptsHint: Others see when you've read their messages. If off, your devices still stay in sync.
settings.privacy.removeMetadataHint: Before a file is sent, this device removes where and when it was made, the camera or phone and its serial number, the software used, and its editing history. Photos: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, HEIC and AVIF. Videos: MP4, MOV, 3GP, WebM and MKV. Drawings: SVG. Other files are sent as they are.
settings.privacy.showOnlineHint: If off, people see “last seen recently” instead of your status.
settings.profile.lead: Only members of {server} can see this. Your server stores it encrypted.
settings.security.browserKeyWarning: Browsers can't lock Zuna's local data to your login, so anyone who can copy this browser's profile can read it. On a computer others use, sign out when you're done, or use the desktop app.
settings.security.recoveryKeyHint: Create a new key if you've lost the old one or think someone saw it. The old key stops working immediately.
settings.security.securityKeyHint: Compare it with friends to make sure nobody is intercepting your messages.
settings.title: Settings
